subject: bia
title: BIA.------AFI.
description: Diagram in PCC-25, the first of two on book p341, where Braxton specifies the AFI(1) and AFI(2) bifurcation in diagram form. (C)BIA (the *concept* of bi-aitional, the masculine/feminine dual-principle structure) is crossed with AFI (affinity insight). The diagram contains all three AFI nodes — AFI, AFI-1, AFI-2 — making the affinity-insight bifurcation diagrammatic. BIA → (R)C-INFO (the reality of composite information) → ACT (activism) → AFI. AFI has a *dashed* edge to AFI-2 (the second-degree affinity insight, the celebration/composite-knowingness principle). AFI-2 → SOC-RT (social reality), with a *dashed* edge from SOC-RT to AFI-1 (the first-degree affinity insight, the affirmation/transformation principle). AFI-1 → PR-TRS (primary transition). C-INFO also → PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) → COS-P (cosmic particulars) → DYM-F (dynamic functionalism), and PROG-CONT → (R)ATTN (the reality of attraction). Structural argument: bi-aitionalism crossed with affinity insight produces a chain through real composite information into activism into affinity insight, which then bifurcates: the dashed edge to AFI(2) registers that celebration/composite-knowingness is conditional on the activism's character; AFI(2) produces social reality; the dashed edge from social reality to AFI(1) registers that the affirmation/transformation principle is conditionally activated by social reality; AFI(1) produces primary transition. The diagram thus diagrams *how transformation actually arrives*: bi-aitionalism → real composite information → activism → AFI → AFI(2) → social reality → AFI(1) → primary transition, with two conditional steps. The parallel progressional-continuance chain produces cosmic particulars and dynamic functionalism, plus real attraction, as the non-transformational outputs.
